description: DentAI Quality Ledger. Append-only evidence registry of defects, test gaps and observations. Entries conform to .control/quality-ledger.schema.json.

entries.reproduction: Login as Dr Disc OneA/4711 -> type observation -> Add -> Sign Out -> login again -> workspace empty, 0 lines, no server record. Reproduced 2/2.
entries.expected: Logging out mid-consult must never destroy unsaved clinical work (explicit intent comment in src/App.tsx handleLogout).
entries.actual: Sign Out destroys the unsaved scratchpad note; neither persisted nor restored on re-login. Scratchpad is only persisted on completion (Rule 18).
entries.rootCause: App.handleLogout clears setConsultations([]) and setSelectedConsultation(null) while the 'chair-active' scratchpad is only persisted on completion; preservation claim only partially implemented (1F S-17).
entries.regressionTest: Manual only: Sign Out with an unsaved scratchpad note -> "Unsaved Clinical Work" confirmation; "Stay Signed In" cancels, "Discard & Sign Out" proceeds. No automated client test exists for the modal.
entries.recommendedAction: IMPLEMENTED in the working tree (uncommitted, branch fix/qle-2026-0042-api-error-json): Sign Out now confirms when unsaved clinical work exists, and App.tsx no longer claims scratchpad persistence it does not do. This is the explicit-discard option ONLY. HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED: must an in-progress scratchpad survive logout (persist/flush to the server or sessionStorage) or is confirm-and-discard the accepted product behaviour? Not merged, not released.
entries.releaseRisk: Silent clinical data loss on a routine action (sign out); directly contradicts the product's own safety intent comment.

entries.reproduction: With consultation 'A B' on server for today -> Tools > Past Patient Records -> click row -> banner shows 'In-Chair Patient' with empty note. Reproduced 2/2.
entries.expected: Clicking a History Hub record opens that patient's record.
entries.actual: Reopen silently lands on the 'In-Chair Patient' scratchpad instead of the selected patient. The consultation is filtered out of encountersForDate by a date-format mismatch; self-healing focus gate resets; effective encounter falls back to the scratchpad. No error surfaced.
entries.rootCause: encountersForDate four-way date heuristic (ChairsideWorkspace.tsx:407-431) silently drops records matching none of the date formats (1F S-9).
entries.regressionTest: tests/date.test.ts — clinicDayKeyOfStoredDate (ISO day, ISO timestamp, "Sep 28", "Sep 28, 2026", "September 28 2026", DD/MM/YYYY, null for uninterpretable). The UI journey itself is covered only by scripts/phase12-ui-smoke.ts (roster/badge behaviour), not by an automated reopen-after-date-change test.
entries.recommendedAction: IMPLEMENTED in the working tree (uncommitted): stored dates are compared as canonical clinic-day keys (new clinicDayKeyOfStoredDate) and the focus effect no longer clears or switches the active patient when the record exists but is not on the selected day — it keeps focus and shows a turnover warning instead. HUMAN REVIEW REQUIRED before merge: protected surfaces 1 (patient identity) and 2 (consultation identity). Not merged, not released.
entries.releaseRisk: Wrong-patient surface class: clinician believes they are viewing the selected patient; combined with any write path this is a mis-attribution risk.

entries.reproduction: Create consultation without patient name fields via API -> satisfy grounding+consent+version gates -> POST sign -> 500; immediate retry -> 409 REPLAY. Full transcripts in evidence.
entries.expected: Sign succeeds when all approval gates pass, or fails with a machine-readable refusal without consuming the replay nonce.
entries.actual: 500 TypeError (unguarded firstName/lastName.trim(), src/lib/attestation.ts:37); the replay nonce is consumed BEFORE the crash (signOffValidation.ts:210-216), so retry gets 409 REPLAY while no seal was persisted. Sign-off dead-ends on an easily reachable record shape. Fail-closed (no invalid seal) but blocks finalization.
entries.rootCause: Unguarded .trim() on optional name fields in attestation seal building; nonce consumption ordered before seal persistence.
entries.regressionTest: tests/signOffValidation.test.ts — "Sign-off robustness (QLE-2026-0003)" (nameless record signs without a 500; a refused sign-off does not consume the nonce; a genuine duplicate is still refused) + tests/uiSafety.test.ts T8/T8b (refusal leaves the nonce retryable; an already-sealed record is refused 409 REPLAY).
entries.recommendedAction: IMPLEMENTED in the working tree (uncommitted): (a) buildCanonicalTextDigest guards absent firstName/lastName instead of throwing; (b) the request nonce is consumed only after the seal is durably persisted, so a refusal stays retryable. Full local suite green (1153 passed / 0 failed). HUMAN REVIEW REQUIRED before merge (sign-off surface). Residual: the in-memory consumed-nonce set is per instance, so the durable persisted-seal check remains the primary replay defence.
entries.releaseRisk: Sign-off hard-fails with 500 and burns the replay nonce; clinicians cannot finalize records with missing name fields.

entries.reproduction: Add Walk-in -> Confirm Consent & Record -> switch to Patient Records tab -> back to Today's Schedule -> no Finish control. Reproduced 1/1 (mic permission persistence made a second run redundant; flagged for re-verification).
entries.expected: Mid-recording navigation preserves a way to finish the consult; recording state survives the tab switch.
entries.actual: TopSurgeryBar renders only while recordingItem (component state) is set; tab switch unmounts it; persisted roster status stays 'recording'; on return the card offers only 'Reset' (silently discards the recording) instead of a Finish control.
entries.rootCause: Encounters are a UI-derived projection rebuilt from client-only sets each render (1F S-1); the only Finish control lives in a component that unmounts.
entries.regressionTest: E2E: navigate away and back mid-recording; assert a Finish control exists and roster status is consistent.
entries.recommendedAction: Stage 2: re-verify live (2nd reproduction), then persist recording state server-side or in a scoped store.
entries.releaseRisk: Recording stranded with no finish path; only recovery is a silent Reset that discards the consult.

entries.reproduction: createCanonicalClinicalFact with status:'PERFORMED' + temporal:'future' -> admitted as canonical with validationState:'valid'; speaker:'robot' + evidenceType:'made_up' -> admitted valid. Demonstrated in evidence2/enum-attack-result.json.
entries.expected: The status x temporal matrix and epistemic guards reject enum-invalid candidates regardless of casing or unknown enum values.
entries.actual: No runtime enum-membership validation at the ClinicalFact trust boundary; guards use === against lowercase literals, so casing and arbitrary enum strings bypass the matrix. Stray top-level teeth/surfaces are silently dropped.
entries.rootCause: Matrix uses === against lowercase enum literals with no preceding enum-membership validation (src/types/clinicalFact.ts, clinicalFactMigration.ts:203-300).
entries.regressionTest: tests/clinicalFactContract.test.ts > "enum membership at the ClinicalFact trust boundary (QLE-2026-0005)" (4 cases: uppercase status+temporal pair refused via normalise-then-matrix, invented speaker/evidenceType/status refused, recognised case/whitespace variant normalised to the canonical member, valid candidate still admissible).
entries.recommendedAction: IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-30 (uncommitted): membership tables + checkFactEnumMember added to src/types/clinicalFact.ts (Record<Union,true> so the tables cannot drift from the unions) and enforced in createCanonicalClinicalFact (src/lib/clinicalFactMigration.ts) BEFORE the status x temporal matrix. A recognised case/whitespace variant is normalised to the canonical member (so a real assertion is not discarded and the matrix then applies); an unknown/absent value is refused, fail closed. Verified: tsc -b --noEmit exit 0; clinicalFactContract 36/36; the 14 fact/grounding/evaluation suites 204/204. NOT released: this is ClinicalFact semantics (HIGH clinical risk, gated). Remaining human step: independent review, then merge + deploy. Stage-3 residual, NOT fixed here: stray top-level teeth/surfaces are still silently dropped (separate concern; needs its own finding).
entries.releaseRisk: Unfixed, a malformed LLM extraction could mint a canonical fact the matrix was meant to forbid while labelling it valid. Fixed locally: the matrix can no longer be bypassed by casing or an unknown enum value. Residual after fix: the extractor prompt still emits free-form enums; a casing variant is now normalised rather than surfaced, so a systematic extractor regression in enum spelling is silent instead of loud (the facts still carry their true semantics).

entries.reproduction: Two POST /api/notes/jobs with a non-UUID consultationId -> two 202s, two jobs, usage metered twice (1->2), two durable consultations (5b0463a1-..., ed4e3cf8-...) in the temp store. Live evidence captured.
entries.expected: Duplicate job submission for the same consultation converges on one job and one record.
entries.actual: Job id is derived from the client's consultationId only when UUID-shaped (server.ts:1998-2010); non-UUID ids get a fresh crypto.randomUUID() per call, so the Phase-9 dedupe never fires. The chairside client persists encounters under non-UUID ids ('consult-<ts>', 'chair-active'), so the real UI path likely does not converge either.
entries.rootCause: Two causes, one shape: the client minted non-UUID record ids per lifecycle stage (`sched-<ts>-<i>`, `chair-active`, `consult-<ts>`) and the server derives the durable job id from the client id only when it is UUID-shaped. A non-UUID id therefore produced a fresh job per call, so nothing could converge. The QLE-2026-0015 id-collision gate then made the converged case fail instead, which is why the two defects could not be fixed separately.
entries.regressionTest: tests/appointmentId.test.ts + tests/server.test.ts ("treats a repeated seating write as a retry, not a duplicate record" — one record for the same appointment id sent twice)
entries.recommendedAction: Implemented by the appointment-identity change (QLE-2026-0048): ids are minted once at seating as canonical UUIDs and a repeated create for an appointment the caller already owns is idempotent, so retries converge on one record instead of duplicating or 409-ing. Review with 0048.
entries.releaseRisk: Duplicate retries create duplicate clinical records and double-spend the clinic's AI allowance.

entries.reproduction: Static only: transcription persist overwrites consultation.transcript via deps.updateConsultation with no version bump, revision append, grounding recompute, or signed-immutability check. Behavioural re-verification flagged as highest-value for DETERMINISTIC_TESTER.
entries.expected: Every consultation write path enforces versioning, revisions, grounding recompute, and signed-record immutability.
entries.actual: Transcript can be replaced on a record whose groundingAudit was computed over the OLD transcript, and can write over a SIGNED record's transcript (seal digest covers findings, not transcript) without any audit event. Concurrent transcription + clinician edit is last-writer-wins on the whole document.
entries.rootCause: recordGovernance covers only POST/PUT /api/consultations and two read routes; three server-side writers bypass it (1F S-3).
entries.regressionTest: Transcribe concurrently with a clinician PUT; transcribe against a signed record; assert version/revision/immutability behaviour.
entries.recommendedAction: Stage 2: route all server-side writers through one governance path.
entries.releaseRisk: Signed record's evidentiary basis can change post-attestation without any audit event; grounding approval can silently diverge from content.

entries.reproduction: Static timing analysis: sign route validates at version V then persistSeal does load->spread->write; a concurrent PUT that loaded existing before the seal landed writes the merged body without the seal. JSON store path has the same read-modify-write shape.
entries.expected: Either the PUT is refused once a seal exists, or the seal write is atomic with respect to concurrent PUTs.
entries.actual: Neither preserves the other: a concurrent PUT can clobber the seal; client state says SIGNED while the server record is unsigned, and the record becomes re-editable (seal loss = immutability loss).
entries.rootCause: persistSeal read-modify-write is not atomic (server.ts ~433-457); PUT immutability check and write are two separate loads (1C ISSUE-1C-06).
entries.regressionTest: Concurrent sign + PUT race on the same consultation; assert the seal survives and the PUT is refused.
entries.recommendedAction: Stage 2: make seal persistence atomic (single-store conditional write) and re-check immutability inside the PUT write.
entries.releaseRisk: Signed record silently loses its seal and becomes re-editable; server/client disagreement on signed state.

entries.reproduction: tests/consultationList.test.ts > "consultationList — poll vs in-flight save (QLE-2026-0009)": a poll response issued before a save carries the record's OLD copy (recordVersion 3) while the in-flight save holds version 4; merged without the preserve rule the poll reverts to 3. That reverted client state is what seeded the next PUT and produced the 409 STALE_WRITE loop.
entries.expected: Poll refresh preserves optimistic local fields (transcript, findings, recordVersion) for in-flight saves.
entries.actual: A finalization save resolving after the poll request was issued is reverted on the next poll response; the reverted record seeds the next PUT with an old expectedVersion -> self-inflicted STALE_WRITE loop until reconcile.
entries.rootCause: The 30s roster poll (src/App.tsx fetchConsultations) rebuilt the whole list as (local cache + server records, server last) and replaced React state unconditionally, with no notion of a save that had been sent but not settled. A response resolving in that window reverted the in-flight record's fields — transcript, findings, recordVersion — to the server's older copy; the reverted record then supplied an old expectedVersion to the next PUT.
entries.regressionTest: tests/consultationList.test.ts (3 cases): server data still wins for records with no in-flight save (cross-device sync preserved); a record whose save is in flight keeps its local fields and recordVersion instead of reverting, with a negative control showing the pre-fix merge reverts to the old version; server-only and local-only records are both kept with a stable order.
entries.recommendedAction: IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-30 (uncommitted): new mergeConsultationLists(local, server, preserve) in src/lib/consultationList.ts documents the rule; src/App.tsx tracks ids whose save has not settled (inFlightSaveIdsRef, added before the PUT/POST and removed in a finally block so a 409, queue-for-retry, thrown error or early return all release it) and passes the live store records for those ids as the preserve set. The poll now cannot revert an unsettled save. Verified: tsc -b --noEmit exit 0; consultationList 10/10; the 9-file client set 167/167. Stage-3 residual, NOT fixed here: the mirror is still a single localStorage key shared by every tab (QLE-2026-0010) — this fix bounds the damage of a cross-tab overwrite but does not reconcile it.
entries.releaseRisk: Unfixed, a clinician's in-flight edit is reverted by a poll tick, and the reverted record is then written back over the server copy or rejected as stale — the clinician sees their work disappear with no explanation and may re-apply it onto a conflicting version. Fixed locally for the same-tab poll path.

entries.reproduction: Static: two tabs write the same localStorage key 'dentai:consultations' with independently merged maps on each 30s poll; no 'storage' event listener exists to reconcile cross-tab writes.
entries.expected: Cross-tab consultation cache writes are reconciled; the newest state wins.
entries.actual: Classic lost-update on the shared cache: tab1's newer local buffer is overwritten by tab2's stale merge and vice versa; surfaces as flickering transcript history and worst-case a save built on the older record shape.
entries.rootCause: Both tabs write the same localStorage key from independently merged maps with no cross-tab reconciliation (1C ISSUE-1C-12).
entries.regressionTest: Two-tab test: assert no lost update on the shared cache.
entries.recommendedAction: Stage 2: storage-event reconciliation or BroadcastChannel, or drop the localStorage mirror.
entries.releaseRisk: Stale record shape can seed a save in the other tab, corrupting the shared view of the record.

entries.reproduction: Static: refresh mid-finalization wipes React state; post-reload retry within the server's 130s in-flight window gets 409 GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS and silently returns undefined; the local transcript snapshot is gone.
entries.expected: Post-reload the note either exists or is visibly re-runnable.
entries.actual: Encounter renders 'ready'; the user sees 'nothing happened' for up to ~2 minutes; the transcript snapshot that fed the original attempt is lost (only uploaded 5s audio slices persist).
entries.rootCause: Finalization orchestration is client-memory-only (1C ISSUE-1C-11; 1E F-1E2-4); no beforeunload guard; server in-flight gate outlives client state.
entries.regressionTest: Refresh during finalization; assert visible recoverable state instead of silent 409.
entries.recommendedAction: Stage 2: surface 409 GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS to the UI and reconcile on job completion.
entries.releaseRisk: Clinician abandons finalization believing it did nothing; duplicate-retry pressure (compounded by QLE-0006).

entries.reproduction: Deterministic at the logic level (tests/consultationList.test.ts > "negative control: the pre-fix pattern ... loses the first save"): two saves each computed from the same captured list leave the first save's entry at its pre-save value. In the app both handlers were created in one render, so clicking patient B before patient A's PUT resolved produced exactly that snapshot.
entries.expected: Concurrent saves for different encounters do not lose updates in client state.
entries.actual: Lost update in client state (App.tsx handleSaveConsultation builds from a stale closure consultations array) that then round-trips to the server on the next save.
entries.rootCause: src/App.tsx handleSaveConsultation derived the next list from the `consultations` array captured by the render that created the handler (const index = consultations.findIndex(...); let newList = [...consultations]; setConsultations(newList)), and the local-cache mirror plus the post-save server echo were computed from the same captured value. Any two writes whose handlers shared a render started from the same pre-update snapshot; the second setConsultations reverted the first save, and the reverted list was written to localStorage and round-tripped to the server on the next save.
entries.regressionTest: tests/consultationList.test.ts (7 cases): upsert replaces in place / prepends new / never mutates its input; the store's read() is synchronously in sync with the last apply(); a functional updater receives the current list; both overlapping saves survive and the next save does not resurrect a list missing the first; plus a negative control encoding the old snapshot pattern so it cannot be reintroduced silently.
entries.recommendedAction: IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-30 (uncommitted): new src/lib/consultationList.ts (createConsultationListStore + upsertConsultation) holds the list outside React and passes the live list to every updater; src/App.tsx routes all eleven list writes through applyConsultations and reads consultationsStore.current.read() at save time (including the post-save server echo and the 409 reconciliation, which now merge into the live list instead of the captured one). Verified: tsc -b --noEmit exit 0; consultationList 7/7; supportIssue (imports App) 5/5; uiSafety 9-file client set 167/167. Stage-3 residual, NOT fixed here: the 30s roster poll still replaces the whole array (QLE-2026-0009), and the same store is not yet used to reconcile the poll against in-flight saves.
entries.releaseRisk: Unfixed, a clinician switching patients while a save is in flight loses the earlier note from client state; the loss is mirrored to localStorage and then pushed to the server on the next save, so a documented note could be overwritten with an older copy. Fixed locally: client state can no longer revert a completed local save.

entries.reproduction: Static: an utterance appended between the state update and the 2s debounce flush can be flushed onto the wrong patient's save; refs update in useEffect after render, so a switch in the same tick as an utterance reads the OLD encounter (one-render staleness).
entries.expected: Each utterance is attributed to the encounter it was spoken under.
entries.actual: Rapid A->B->A switching with live speech can attribute the final utterance of A to B's save object.
entries.rootCause: pendingSaveConsultationRef holds only the last consultation object built; ref-sync is one render behind (1C ISSUE-1C-16).
entries.regressionTest: Rapid switch with utterance in the debounce window; assert transcript attribution.
entries.recommendedAction: Stage 2: bind utterances to encounter id at capture time, not at flush time.
entries.releaseRisk: Cross-patient transcript contamination in the clinical record.

entries.reproduction: POST /api/consultations {} -> 201 durable record with consent.obtainedAt:'' and no transcript. Reproduced in both 1E passes at this SHA (T15 re-check).
entries.expected: Creation-side validation enforces required fields per the clinical contract.
entries.actual: Empty-body consultation accepted (201); a record can exist unsigned-but-structured with blank consent. The sign gate refuses it downstream (422 EMPTY_NOTE) so no unsafe sign path was demonstrated, but creation-side validation is more permissive than the clinical contract implies.
entries.rootCause: No required-field gate on the POST route.
entries.regressionTest: tests/server.test.ts — "consultation create contract (QLE-2026-0014 / QLE-2026-0015)": empty body and a bare id/date shell are refused 400 CONSULTATION_REQUIRED_FIELDS; a minimal real consultation and a nameless transcript-bearing consultation are still accepted 201.
entries.recommendedAction: IMPLEMENTED in the working tree (uncommitted): POST /api/consultations refuses a body that documents neither a patient identity nor any clinical content (400 CONSULTATION_REQUIRED_FIELDS). The gate is deliberately narrow (name/patientId OR transcript, patientSummary, note or any non-empty finding). HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED: confirm the required-field set is the intended clinical minimum. HUMAN REVIEW REQUIRED before merge (consultation identity).
entries.releaseRisk: Blank-consent records accumulate; downstream gates are the only line of defence.

entries.reproduction: Duplicate POST with a client-supplied existing id silently overwrites the stored record (JSON path, server.ts:3744-3751) with 201 - no version/ownership conflict check. Client callers mint id-collision-prone ids (sched-/chairside-/consult-<Date.now()>).
entries.expected: Id collision returns a conflict (409) or is ignored (Postgres ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING); both modes agree.
entries.actual: JSON mode overwrites with 201; Postgres ignores; the two storage modes disagree. Two browsers importing a daysheet in the same millisecond mint the same id; JSON-mode POST replaces the existing record.
entries.rootCause: JSON POST path upserts by id without conflict check; client id minting uses Date.now() (1F S-4).
entries.regressionTest: tests/server.test.ts — id collision returns 409 CONSULTATION_ID_CONFLICT and the stored record is unchanged; JSON persistence now uses insertConsultationDeduped (first write wins) so the backstop cannot overwrite either.
entries.recommendedAction: IMPLEMENTED in the working tree (uncommitted): a supplied id that already exists is refused 409 in BOTH storage modes (dbConsultationExistsById for Postgres, global id scan for JSON mode) and the JSON path no longer overwrites by index. HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED: 409-refuse vs upsert-on-collision. INTERACTION: this gate is what now makes the QLE-2026-0006 convergence fix require a client save-path change — a converged durable record would make the client POST collide and get 409. Do not release 0015 and 0006 independently without resolving that.
entries.releaseRisk: Silent replacement of an existing clinical record with 201 - data loss disguised as success.

entries.reproduction: POST /api/patients with malformed DOB -> 201; dateOfBirth field silently ignored (route reads 'dob' only).
entries.expected: Malformed DOB rejected; dateOfBirth accepted and stored.
entries.actual: Malformed DOB accepted; a submitted dateOfBirth is silently dropped - silent identity-data loss weakening patient-resolution policy.
entries.rootCause: Route reads 'dob' only with no schema validation (FINDING-1B-203).
entries.regressionTest: tests/patientIdentity.test.ts — "patient date of birth parsing (QLE-2026-0016)": dob and dateOfBirth are both read; malformed and impossible dates are refused 400 INVALID_DOB; an absent DOB stays absent.
entries.recommendedAction: IMPLEMENTED in the working tree (uncommitted): parsePatientDob accepts dob ?? dateOfBirth, requires a strict YYYY-MM-DD real calendar date, and both POST /api/patients and POST /api/patients/resolve return 400 INVALID_DOB. HUMAN REVIEW REQUIRED before merge (patient identity).
entries.releaseRisk: Patient charts silently missing DOB; weakens the DOB-conflict safety rule in identity resolution.

entries.reproduction: Two POST /api/notes/jobs with a converging UUID consultationId -> one job, one consultation, but usage metered twice (used 5 then 6).
entries.expected: Deduplicated submission does not meter twice.
entries.actual: Both calls increment the usage snapshot even when the dedupe collapses them to one job; a retry loop can burn the daily allowance with duplicate submissions that generate nothing new.
entries.rootCause: Usage metering increments before the dedupe check (F-1E2-2). 2026-09-29 static review NARROWED this: job submission is NOT metered (createAiMetering is wired with recordUsage:false at server.ts:401-406); usage is recorded only on successful completion (server.ts:1759). The duplicate path therefore cannot double-count via the dedupe alone. The surviving mechanism is a concurrency race: both requests await tickNoteJobs(true) (server.ts:2057) and can process the SAME queued job with no claim/lease lock in JSON mode, so one job can complete twice. NOT yet confirmed by a concurrency probe.
entries.regressionTest: Duplicate job submission -> single usage increment. (Needs a CONCURRENT two-request probe; the existing sequential test at tests/clinicalPipelineReliability.test.ts:226 asserts one job in the store but never asserts the usage count.)
entries.recommendedAction: Evidence first: write a concurrent duplicate-submission probe asserting exactly one usage increment. Do NOT implement from the static read. NOTE the race is broader than metering - a shared queued job processed twice could also double-generate/double-persist clinical content, which is a clinical-content-integrity question and would need the same human gate as QLE-0006/0007.
entries.releaseRisk: Retry loops exhaust the clinic's daily AI allowance without generating notes.

entries.reproduction: Static timing: client polls a queued job for only 25s (ChairsideWorkspace.tsx:2464) then silently falls back to the offline draft; server quota backoff starts at 45s and caps at 6min.
entries.expected: Client waits out the server's retry ladder or reconciles when the durable job completes.
entries.actual: On any quota blip the client abandons polling before the first server retry fires, renders the offline draft, and the durable job later completes server-side - two different notes for one encounter with no UI signal that the abandoned job completed.
entries.rootCause: 25s client poll deadline < 45s minimum server backoff (F-1E2-3).
entries.regressionTest: tests/noteJobs.test.ts — "client poll budget vs the worker retry ladder (QLE-2026-0018)": the client deadline must exceed the worker first-retry backoff, must not exceed the attempt budget, and the poll interval must be bounded.
entries.recommendedAction: IMPLEMENTED in the working tree (uncommitted): NOTE_JOB_CLIENT_POLL (deadline = 2 x backoffBaseMs + 5s = 95s, interval 2s) lives next to the retry ladder it has to outlive, and both note surfaces (ChairsideWorkspace, DayScheduleQueue) use it instead of local 25s/85s literals. Partial by design: editor reconciliation with a durable job that completes after the deadline is a separate, larger change. Not committed.
entries.releaseRisk: Clinician edits an offline draft while the durable record gets a different note - divergence with no signal.

entries.reproduction: Static: 4 rapid Add clicks in ~100ms -> 4 identical Dialogue rows, counter '4 lines recorded'. Reproduced 2/2 live.
entries.expected: Rapid clicks are debounced or deduplicated at capture.
entries.actual: Duplicate transcript rows are recorded; the note draft de-duplicates, but the grounding layer treats the transcript as evidence and duplicates pollute it.
entries.rootCause: No capture-side debounce/dedupe on the Add control.
entries.regressionTest: 4 rapid Add clicks -> 1 row (or visible coalescing).
entries.recommendedAction: Stage 2: debounce capture; dedupe at the transcript layer before it feeds grounding.
entries.releaseRisk: Transcript evidence polluted with duplicates can skew grounding and omission detection.

entries.reproduction: Static: sign gate's canonicalContent (signOffValidation.ts:66-97) and attestation's buildCanonicalTextDigest (attestation.ts:37-90) implement the same canonicalization with a real divergence - attestation includes ADA_CODES, the sign gate does not.
entries.expected: One canonicalization owns both digest call sites.
entries.actual: Two divergent digest implementations; today benign (seal built and verified by the same function), but any cross-comparison of sign-gate digest vs seal digest will falsely match records differing only in ADA codes.
entries.rootCause: Duplicated canonicalization logic (1F S-5).
entries.regressionTest: Records differing only in ADA codes must produce different digests in both implementations.
entries.recommendedAction: Stage 2: extract one canonical digest module used by both.
entries.releaseRisk: Future sign-gate/seal digest comparison can falsely equal distinct records.

entries.reproduction: Static: signOffTargetVersion and handleSignOffActiveNote fall back to consultations.find(...)?.recordVersion (client-held state mirrored to localStorage) instead of serverRecordVersions only.
entries.expected: Sign-off versions come ONLY from server responses (Phase 12E contract comment).
entries.actual: Fallback reads client-cached versions; failure mode is benign (server refuses 409 STALE_VERSION and updates the map), so this is a contract inconsistency rather than a confirmed defect.
entries.rootCause: Contract-vs-implementation drift in the version source (1F S-2).
entries.regressionTest: Sign-off with a stale cached version -> 409 handled gracefully (existing behaviour).
entries.recommendedAction: Stage 2: align implementation with the Phase 12E contract or amend the contract.
entries.releaseRisk: None demonstrated; noise-level 409s possible.

entries.reproduction: curl /api/records -> 200 SPA HTML; bogus-id reads and malformed JSON / payload-limit errors return HTML (Express default) instead of JSON. Reproduced by 1B (Phase 1) and 1E.
entries.expected: Unknown /api/* paths return 404 JSON; parse/limit errors return JSON error bodies.
entries.actual: 200 SPA HTML for unknown API paths (F-1B-1 / FINDING-1B-205 / F-1E-3); HTML error pages for 400/413 (F-1E-2). Clients cannot distinguish 'not found' from 'found'; error contract inconsistent.
entries.rootCause: SPA get * fallback mounted before an API 404 handler; no JSON error renderer for parse/limit errors.
entries.regressionTest: tests/server.test.ts > 'DentAI Server - API 404 fallback (QLE-2026-0022)' — unknown GET/nested/POST /api/* -> 404 JSON with code API_NOT_FOUND; /api/health, / and /chairside unaffected. NOT covered: malformed body -> 400 JSON (separate deferred finding).
entries.recommendedAction: DONE (Stage 2): API-scoped terminal 404/JSON handler added above the SPA fallback in server.ts. Malformed-JSON/payload-limit JSON rendering was deliberately NOT folded into this fix and remains a separate deferred finding.

entries.API: any /api/* route (malformed JSON body, or body over the 1MB express.json() limit)
entries.reproduction: POST /api/consultations with a malformed JSON body ('{"broken": ') -> answered with an HTML error page instead of JSON; same for a body over the 1MB limit. Originally observed as F-1E-2. Re-confirmed 2026-09-29: server.ts contained NO error-handling middleware at all, so body-parser errors fell through to Express's built-in HTML handler.
entries.expected: Anything under /api is answered with machine-parsable JSON, matching the QLE-2026-0022 contract.
entries.actual: Malformed JSON -> HTML 400 page; oversized body -> HTML 413 page. The same contract break QLE-2026-0022 fixed for unknown paths, for two different failure modes. Deliberately NOT folded into the QLE-2026-0022 fix.
entries.rootCause: No error-handling middleware registered anywhere in server.ts; express.json({limit:'1mb'}) at line 205 raises entity.parse.failed / entity.too.large with nothing to render them as JSON.
entries.regressionTest: tests/server.test.ts — malformed JSON body -> 400 INVALID_JSON; oversized body -> 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE; unexpected handler failure -> 500 INTERNAL_ERROR, all JSON.
entries.recommendedAction: IMPLEMENTED + regression-tested (commit bf07bb8 on branch fix/qle-2026-0042-api-error-json; full suite 1153 passed / 0 failed). NOT DEPLOYED: production probe 8 in reports/releases/PRODUCTION-PROBE-2026-09-30.md shows the live app still answers a malformed JSON POST with the Express default HTML 400 page. Needs commit + push + PR + deploy.
entries.releaseRisk: Monitoring and machine clients cannot parse API failures; inconsistent with the contract QLE-2026-0022 established.

entries.journey: Dentist opens a patient whose date of birth came off a pasted day sheet and asks for the note
entries.reproduction: POST /api/generate-notes with intakeData.dob = "11/10/1976" — the value the operatory banner displays, because the schedule parser stores the pasted day sheet verbatim (ChairsideWorkspace.tsx:1967) and the banner renders it raw (OperatoryPatientBanner.tsx:124) — returns 400 "Date of birth must be in YYYY-MM-DD format." POST /api/notes/jobs accepts the same body, so the client (ChairsideWorkspace.tsx:2471) falls through to the job queue and logs only "Direct note generation status: 400, falling back to background job queue."
entries.expected: A date of birth the product itself captured and displays is understood by the synchronous note path, and one canonical form is stored.
entries.actual: Every note for a patient with a non-ISO date of birth silently leaves the synchronous path for the durable job queue; the two generation paths disagreed about what is valid, and nothing surfaced to the clinician.
evidence: tests/server.test.ts > should not refuse a day-sheet dob for its format (QLE-2026-0043)
entries.rootCause: server.ts enforced /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ on intakeData.dob in POST /api/generate-notes, while POST /api/notes/jobs validated no date of birth at all, and the client stores and renders the day-sheet string verbatim.
entries.regressionTest: tests/dob.test.ts — 13 cases (ISO, DD/MM, MM/DD, named month, two-digit year, leap day, impossible/future/pre-1900 dates, absent stays absent, canonical round-trip). tests/server.test.ts — DOB pair: unreadable value still 400; day-sheet value no longer refused (returns 200 with the mock provider). Verified locally: tsc --noEmit exit 0; 34/34 across tests/dob.test.ts + tests/patientIdentity.test.ts.
entries.recommendedAction: DONE on branch fix/qle-2026-0042-api-error-json: src/lib/dob.ts normaliser (clinic policy for prompt context, strict for patient identity) wired into /api/generate-notes (canonicalises intakeData.dob), /api/notes/jobs (normalises when readable, never newly refuses) and parsePatientDob (strict — a two-way date is refused for identity). REMAINING: the client still stores and renders the raw day-sheet string; make it store ISO with a display formatter so referral letters, progress notes and the attestation digest all carry one form.
entries.releaseRisk: Low: the synchronous path admits more inputs than before and one refusal message changed; no stored record is rewritten.

entries.screen: Chairside workspace — saving a recorded consultation
entries.journey: Dentist records the appointment, then the client saves the record (POST for a new encounter, PUT for every later edit)
entries.reproduction: src/server/recordGovernance.ts:148 refuses any consultation write whose body carries a transcript and no consent.obtainedAt. No client code ever sets consent on a consultation: the field is declared as required for new records in types.ts:298 and is never populated anywhere in src/, because chairside consent is captured as the FLAT fields consentObtained / consentCapturedAt / consentPractitionerId on the day-schedule item (DayScheduleQueue.tsx:79-107) and is not carried onto the consultation. Production enforces the gate: GET /api/health reports configuration.blocking = 0 (every fatal/required key set, since a required key that is missing or empty would be blocking) and GET /api/auth/profiles answers 404 DIRECTORY_DISABLED, which proves the operator sets these boolean flags to the documented "true" — the same convention the go-live checklist (docs/operations/au-go-live-checklist.md:53) mandates for DENTAI_REQUIRE_CONSENT.
entries.expected: A record whose AI-assist consent was captured chairside saves, with consent stored in one canonical shape. A record with no consent evidence is refused AND the clinician is told.
entries.actual: 400 CONSENT_REQUIRED permanently, for every transcript-bearing consultation write. App.tsx:664 catches the non-ok response and calls queuePendingSync with no user-visible error, so the note looks saved, stays in the browser, and is retried — and refused — on every load. This matches the reported console exactly: three records x two 400s on /api/consultations/<id>, and no POST failures (a record created before it had a transcript passes the gate, then can never be updated again).
evidence: DevTools capture 2026-09-30 18:51 — six 400s on /api/consultations/<id> (three distinct ids, each twice), production origin/main @ 23768f8
GET /api/health (live, public) — configuration.blocking = 0, advisories = 3 (the three "recommended" keys)
GET /api/auth/profiles (live, public) — 404 DIRECTORY_DISABLED, calibrating flag values to the documented "true"
entries.rootCause: The write gate understands only the nested consent object, while the product captures consent as flat fields; the sign-off gate already accepts both shapes, so the two gates disagree about what consent evidence exists.
entries.regressionTest: NONE YET. The reproduction needs an authenticated write carrying a transcript. Required next: tests/server.test.ts — (a) transcript + no consent evidence -> 400 CONSENT_REQUIRED; (b) transcript + chairside consent evidence -> saved, with the canonical consent stamp persisted.
entries.recommendedAction: NOT FIXED. Highest-value next action on this tree. One change, three parts: (1) recordGovernance accepts the flat chairside evidence the sign gate accepts and normalises it into the canonical consent stamp; (2) the client carries consentObtained / consentCapturedAt / consentPractitionerId from the day-schedule item onto the consultation it saves; (3) a refused save is surfaced to the clinician instead of being silently queued behind a "Saved" state. Separately, confirm with the operator the actual value of DENTAI_REQUIRE_CONSENT in the Vercel environment — the code cannot be probed for it without credentials.
entries.releaseRisk: HIGH if unreviewed: until it is fixed, no recorded appointment persists server-side on a deployment with DENTAI_REQUIRE_CONSENT=true, which is the posture this deployment appears to be in.

entries.screen: Chairside workspace — Clinical Note Canvas, Sign Off
entries.journey: Dentist finishes the appointment and clicks Sign Off
entries.reproduction: Reported chairside: "on clicking sign off nothing happens". Three independent mechanisms in handleSignOffActiveNote (ChairsideWorkspace.tsx:688-741) produce exactly that: (1) line 690 returns with NO message, error or toast when the active record is the in-chair scratchpad (`targetId === chair-active`), so the button is a silent no-op; (2) line 694 refuses locally when no server-stamped recordVersion exists, which is the case for every record whose saves are being refused (QLE-2026-0044) — the refusal renders as an inline note the clinician may read as decoration; (3) line 691's `if (signOffBusyId) return;` guard has no timeout behind it (src/lib/signOffClient.ts sets none and has no AbortController), so one hung request leaves the button permanently dead until reload.
entries.expected: A refused sign-off states why, in the clinician's line of sight, and the control never becomes silently inert.
entries.actual: The click can do nothing at all — no state change, no message — and with saves refused by the consent gate no record can acquire the expectedVersion the sign path requires, so sign-off is unreachable for every recorded appointment.
evidence: DevTools capture 2026-09-30 18:55 (Sign Off present, no signed state, no console entry on click)
server.ts:3869-3875 (400 EXPECTED_VERSION_REQUIRED when expectedVersion is not a number)
entries.rootCause: The sign-off control has three silent failure branches and one permanent one: a scratchpad no-op, a version-less refusal, an unbounded in-flight guard, and the upstream fact that refused saves (consent gate) mean no encounter ever holds a server recordVersion.
entries.regressionTest: NONE. Next: a UI test that clicks Sign Off on (a) a scratchpad encounter, (b) a record with no server version and (c) a refused server sign-off, asserting a visible message in every case; plus a test that an in-flight sign request cannot block a later one indefinitely.
entries.recommendedAction: NOT FIXED. Fix together with QLE-2026-0044: never let Sign Off be a silent no-op (say "this record has not been saved yet" or "finish or discard this in-chair draft"), time-bound the request so the busy guard cannot wedge, and fix the save refusal that removes the version in the first place.
entries.releaseRisk: HIGH for a dentist handover: a note that cannot be signed cannot be an unsigned clinical record.

entries.screen: Chairside workspace — patient transition (Next Patient / pager)
entries.journey: Two appointments are pasted for the same patient name; the dentist works the first, then advances to the second
entries.reproduction: Reported chairside: "when the dentist clicks on the next patient it takes a lot of time to load and eventually when it loads it already has some previous data populated on it". The capture shows the 6:55 PM encounter ("In Operatory", REC 00:00, Start Audio, i.e. nothing recorded yet) displaying the 6:51 PM encounter's dialogue (6:47:39-6:48:38) and the 6:49 PM note, while the banner correctly reads 6:55 PM. The day schedule lists both as Patient 3.
entries.expected: The switch is immediate, and the destination encounter shows only its own content — an empty canvas for an appointment with nothing recorded.
entries.actual: A newly opened appointment can present the previous appointment's transcript and note under its own header and time.
evidence: DevTools capture / screenshot 2026-09-30 18:55 (banner 6:55 PM, dialogue 6:47-6:48, note dated 6:49 PM)
src/components/ChairsideWorkspace.tsx:269-334 (patientEncounters maps one encounter per consultation and reads c.transcript + localLiveTranscripts[c.id])
entries.rootCause: UNRESOLVED. Static reading rules out the two obvious candidates (the transition blocks nothing; an encounter's transcript is read from its own consultation id), which leaves encounter-identity resolution for two appointments that share a patient name — most likely the new appointment resolving to, or being seeded from, the earlier record. Naming it needs a live reproduction with the exact two-line schedule paste.
entries.regressionTest: NONE. Required: a browser test that pastes two appointments for the same patient name, records nothing on the second, and asserts the canvas and dialogue are empty; plus a timing assertion on the transition so a stall cannot reappear unnoticed.
entries.recommendedAction: NOT FIXED — evidence first, per the repo rule. Reproduce locally with the same paste, capture which encounter id the canvas resolves, then fix identity resolution. Do NOT "fix" the transition by clearing buffers speculatively: the retention of a finished encounter's buffers is deliberate (ChairsideWorkspace.tsx:2965-2975).
entries.releaseRisk: HIGH if confirmed: the wrong patient's dialogue on screen is the input to the signed record.

entries.screen: Chairside workspace — operatory patient banner, Walk-In
entries.journey: A patient arrives without an appointment and the dentist adds them as a walk-in
entries.reproduction: Reported chairside: "clicking on this element - Walk-In doesnt add a walk in it just updating the current patient on the screens record." Confirmed in the code: OperatoryPatientBanner declares onOpenWalkIn (line 22), destructures it (line 34) and ChairsideWorkspace passes it (ChairsideWorkspace.tsx:3928, onOpenWalkIn={() => setShowWalkInCard(true)}) — and the banner never references it again. Both walk-in entry points (the empty-state "Walk-In Patient" button and the header "Walk-In" button) call handleOpenInduction, whose submit calls onQuickInductPatient -> handleQuickInductPatient (ChairsideWorkspace.tsx:2262), which updates the ACTIVE consultation in place and toasts "Patient updated: ". The genuine walk-in path (handleAddWalkInToStream, ChairsideWorkspace.tsx:2174 — collision-safe id via generateWalkInId, fresh empty transcript, no fabricated content) is therefore unreachable from the banner.
entries.expected: Adding a walk-in creates a NEW encounter with its own id and no inherited clinical content, and never changes the record of the patient already in the chair.
entries.actual: No walk-in is created. A scheduled patient already on screen is renamed and re-saved under the walk-in's name and date of birth — the wrong patient's identity written onto the chart whose transcript and note will be signed. The clinician sees only "Patient updated: <name>".
evidence: grep onOpenWalkIn src/ — three hits: the prop type, the destructure, the call site. No usage.
entries.rootCause: Two different user intentions (add a walk-in / edit the patient in the chair) were wired to one handler. The walk-in prop was added and plumbed but never connected, so the only reachable path was the in-place edit.
entries.regressionTest: NONE YET — and none of the existing suites can hold this one: the repo has no component-render test infrastructure (no testing-library, no react-dom/server usage in tests/), so a wiring regression here needs a browser assertion in the Playwright smoke harness (scripts/phase12-ui-smoke.ts / phase13a-encounter-safety-smoke.ts): click Walk-In, submit a new name, assert a new encounter exists and the previously open record is unchanged. entries.reproduction: Seat a patient in the chair (Next Patient). The face-to-face audio is a MediaRecorder effect guarded by `if (!authToken || !activeEncounter?.id) return;` — and the in-chair slot is the derived `effectiveEncounter`, so activeEncounter is null and no segment is ever uploaded. Then click Sign Off: `handleSignOffActiveNote` early-returns on `targetId === 'chair-active'` (silent no-op), and even past that guard there is no server-stamped recordVersion because no record exists. Console shows `/api/transcribe` (NO_AUDIO) and `/api/consultations/<id>` failures; the doctor-visible surface shows nothing wrong.
entries.expected: One appointment identity, minted once when the patient is seated and used verbatim by every subsystem (audio namespace, note-job id, transcript buffer, record version, seal). A visit is never renamed mid-life, and an in-chair visit is signable because its record exists from the moment of seating.
entries.actual: A single visit wore up to three different ids — `sched-<ts>-<i>`, `chair-active`, `consult-<ts>` — and the record was renamed at finalisation. `/api/transcribe/audio` refuses audio for a consultation the server has never seen (404 at transcriptionRoutes.ts:156), and a non-UUID id could never converge on one note job (server.ts:2004 `isUuid(consultationId) ? consultationId : crypto.randomUUID()`). The in-chair visit therefore had no identity: no stored audio, no server diarization, no record version, no reachable sign-off, and whatever had been filed under the earlier id was orphaned by the rename.
entries.rootCause: The appointment had no identity of its own. `Consultation` doubled as the visit, the patient label and the clinical document, and its id was re-minted per lifecycle stage, while the in-chair patient was a *derived* object (`effectiveEncounter`) rather than a seated appointment. Every id-keyed subsystem (audio, note jobs, transcript buffers, record versions, the seal) was therefore pointed at a name that changed, and the media recorder — which requires a real activeEncounter — never ran for the in-chair case at all. A second-order consequence made it self-sealing: the record could not be created before it had clinical content (the QLE-2026-0014 gate), but the clinical evidence could not be stored before the record existed.
